The project develops an artificial intelligence system that transforms decision narratives into explicit, verifiable causal models, identifying actions, mechanisms, expected outcomes, evidence, and hypotheses to test. Based on language models and validated against an expert-annotated benchmark, the system will enable comparisons between politicians’ and experts’ narratives, assess their persuasive effects, and analyse their diffusion. It will also support entrepreneurial decision-making, helping startups articulate and test business hypotheses. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Comparative evaluation procedure for n. 3 research contracts - Department of Statistical Sciences “Paolo Fortunati” (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-03 12:00
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/STAT-03 Demografia e statistica sociale

Title of the project: “Networks of Influence in Family Formation – NETFAM” - For decades, European countries have experienced delayed ages for family formation and persistently low birth rates. Economic conditions are not sufficient to explain these phenomena, which have a social dimension that encompasses the social context and environment in which decision-making occurs. NETFAM explores an expansively defined network of potential sources of influence (e.g., family, kin, neighbours, friends, co-workers, and online connections) and studies how they relate to family outcomes (e.g., leaving the parental home, forming a union, having children, separating)..Omissis.

item.description:

Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-01 Economia politica

The project investigates access to justice using administrative data and advanced causal inference methods, with a particular focus on Brazil. It examines how economic circumstances and litigation costs affect court use, the types of claims filed, and the likelihood of success; the role of personal relationships in judicial decisions; and the effects of winning a case on expectations of rights protection and individual behaviour. It also explores the mechanisms underlying these effects and differences across population groups. item.title: Contratto di ricerca: Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna - The distributional impacts of climate change and climate policy (Sc.Sup. S.Anna PISA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-06 12:00
Institution: Sc.Sup. S.Anna PISA, Pisa
Field: Economics and statistics / 13/ECON-01 Economia politica

The researcher will investigate the distributional impacts of climate change and climate policy using a combination of climate econometric and survey-based methods. The analysis will focus on how climate risks and policy interventions affect different socioeconomic groups, sectors, and regions, with particular attention to heterogeneity in exposure and adaptive capacity. Perceptions of the asymmetric consequences of climate change, as well as attitudes toward mitigation and adaptation policies, will also be examined. Strong knowledge of one or more programming languages and data analysis software (e.g., R) is required, along with the ability to manage and analyze complex datasets.
